_comment: FICTIONAL persona for the swe-sponsor-pipeline recipe. EVERY value in this file is your-input: the student's own situation and assumptions, not a record. Edit these to run the pipeline for a different student. v2 (2026-10-02): re-scoped by the author to mid-level AI Engineer roles on the Microsoft AI stack.
summary: an international MS Computer Science student on pre-completion OPT (from mid-October 2026) with about 3.5 years of prior AI-engineering experience, looking for mid-level AI Engineer roles that use the Microsoft AI stack (anywhere in the US, Texas and remote first), at companies that sponsor H-1B visas
_sponsorship_evidence_note: your-input: a company's H-1B history for software OR AI titles counts as sponsorship evidence, because the CSV keeps only a company's top few sponsored titles and AI engineering roles are often filed under software occupations. Postings must still be AI roles (target_families). An AI posting at a company whose record lists only software titles gets the soft 'Possible' tier, so it can reach Consider but not Apply.

preferred_locations._note: your-input preference: postings in Texas or remote are shown first and starred in the report. All US locations stay in. Not a vote, and the scorer's numbers are unchanged.

visa.status: F-1, pre-completion OPT from mid-October 2026; post-completion OPT after the program end date
visa.opt_start_note: opt_start_date is the POST-completion OPT start. Per DHS Study in the States (F-1 OPT page, checked 2026-10-02): 'A student on post-completion OPT can be unemployed for a total of 90 days.' The page does not apply that limit to pre-completion OPT, so the timeline gate counts from post-completion. Pre-completion OPT time reduces the 12 months available after graduation. Confirm with the DSO.

hiring_lag_note: Assumption, not a record: the application-to-offer time this student plans around. No repo record measures hiring lag.
